28.0.0.en: The Lord begins by specifying the condition for obtaining the blessings and avoiding the curses, which is obedience to the commandments of God, which raise His people above the other peoples.

28.1.0.en: In the previous chapter the Lord mentioned the transgressions that bring the curse on those who commit them, and consequently whoever avoids them receives the blessing. In this chapter the Lord gives detail about the nature and character of those curses and blessings, beginning with the blessings in (vv. 3-14). The following appears in this chapter:

28.1.1.en: 1- God's justice and His punishment of everyone who persists in evil.

28.1.2.en: 2- His mercy and His blessings to everyone who obeys Him.

28.1.3.en: 3- The necessity of holding to His commandments in order to keep His grace, for His choosing of His people and His care for them do not prevent punishment from them if they reject His word.

28.1.4.en: 4- His mercy in accepting the repentance of His people if they return to Him after the curses have come upon them, so that He lifts them from them and restores His blessings to them, as appears in (ch. 30).

28.2.0.en: This verse is an extension of the word "overtake" concerning the blessings, which came in the previous verse. The meaning is deep and wonderful: the blessings run to him to overtake him, instead of his running after them to overtake them. Wherever he is, whether in the city practicing an industrial or commercial trade, or in the village practicing agricultural work, the blessings will certainly come to him in all his works.

28.3.0.en: The blessing includes all the product of a person's works, and it is as follows:

28.3.1.en: 1- The fruit of the womb, meaning offspring large in number and good in kind.

28.3.2.en: 2- The fruit of the ground, meaning an abundant harvest.

28.3.3.en: 3- The fruit of the livestock, of cattle and sheep, that is, what the animals bear is also large in number and in good health.

28.3.4.en: In the Divine Liturgy our Church prays the prayers of the Litanies (Awashi) according to the three seasons of the agricultural year: for the Lord to bless the waters of the rivers in the period from 12 Paoni to 9 Paopi; for the crops and the plants of the field in the period from 10 Paopi to 10 Tobi; for the fruits of the earth in the period from 11 Tobi to 11 Paoni. From this we see that the rites of our Church go back in their origins to the words of the Holy Bible, for in these prayers she hopes for God's blessings and His promises of good things.

28.4.0.en: The basket is the vessel in which the fruits are gathered, so blessing it means blessing what is inside it, so that the harvest is abundant.

28.4.1.en: And the kneading trough is the vessel in which the flour is kneaded and becomes bread, so blessing it means abundance of good and satisfaction.

28.5.0.en: "Blessed shall you be when you come in, and blessed shall you be when you go out" means that you will be blessed in your works and in all that you strive for, because carrying out these works requires going out and coming in, so this means that the blessing includes all the activities of life.

28.6.0.en: The Lord gives you victory over everyone who is hostile to you or resists you. If they attack you in great numbers with their soldiers drawn up in ranks and massed against you, that is, coming by one road, He scatters them before you, so that they flee by many roads.

28.6.1.en: Do not be disturbed by the wars of the demons, but take refuge in God by prayer and all the means of grace, and the demons will fear you and flee.

28.7.0.en: The Lord blesses the storehouses of your harvests, so that they are filled with an abundance of good things, and you succeed in all the works you undertake (as was said in the Book of Genesis about Joseph the son of Jacob, "that the LORD made all that he did to prosper in his hand," Gen 39:3). And the blessing in the land that the Lord gives you means settling in the Promised Land and not being exposed to any outside threat.

28.8.0.en: The Lord raises you to a high rank among the peoples, so that you are a holy people, attributed to Him and His own. That is if you keep His commandments and act according to His laws, and then the other peoples will fear you.

28.9.0.en: A repetition of what came in v. 4. The Lord affirms to them a second time that He will bless their offspring and the offspring of their animals and the harvests of their land and the fruits of their trees.

28.10.0.en: God's heavenly treasures are the rains that give abundant harvests to His people, so that they become richer than the peoples around them, and these peoples come to borrow from them, while the people of God borrow from no one because of the abundance of good things they have.

28.11.0.en: And if you listen to the commandments of the Lord you will be superior to all peoples in growth and prosperity, and you will not be at their rear but always lifted above them.

28.12.0.en: The condition for obtaining all these blessings is holding fast to the commandments of God and keeping away from the worship of idols.

28.13.0.en: The cause of all the curses, whether those mentioned here or those mentioned in the previous chapter, is disobedience to the word of God. And these curses are discipline to bring man back to God by repentance.

28.14.0.en: This curse is the opposite of the blessing mentioned in (v. 3), so that failure pursues the person, whether he lives in the city or the village, that is, in all his works.

28.15.0.en: And it is the opposite of what came in (v. 5): instead of the blessing that increases your fruits to fill the basket, and the abundant flour that fills the kneading trough, scarcity and small harvest prevail instead of abundance and satisfaction.

28.16.0.en: And it is the opposite of what came in (v. 4): there will be no blessing in your offspring or in the young of your cattle and sheep, and the blessing is removed from the harvests of your land, so that good things are fewer and you are in want and distress.

28.17.0.en: And it is the opposite of what came in (v. 6): instead of the Lord's blessing your works, you fail in everything you strive for, and failure and disappointment follow you wherever you go and in any place where you settle.

28.18.1.en: They lose their peace and are troubled throughout their lives, and God is angry with them, in addition to the reproach of people, and this trouble continues until their lives quickly end because of the multitude of their sins.

28.19.0.en: The Lord strikes them with epidemics that spread among them and keep hold of them until they destroy most of them, so that their name is blotted out from the land that He gives them.

28.20.0.en: The Lord lists for them the diseases that will seize them to destroy them, which are:

28.20.1.en: Consumption: a disease that affects the lung in man and destroys it, and it is highly contagious.

28.20.2.en: Fever: it is of many kinds, and among its common symptoms is a very high body temperature. Chills: the severe shivering resulting from infection with certain fevers.

28.20.3.en: Inflammation: it affects many systems of the body such as the nerves and muscles, and many diseases result from it, such as rheumatism and others.

28.20.4.en: Drought: the scarcity of water necessary for the needs of man, animals, and crops. In man and animals it may cause death, and in crops it causes withering and the ruin of the harvests.

28.20.5.en: Scorching: the intense heat brought by the hot wind, which may cause the death of people and the ruin of crops and fruits.

28.20.6.en: Withering: severe weakness, the decline of bodily strength, and the loss of activity and vitality.

28.21.0.en: A rhetorical image portraying the scorching heat as if the sky had become bronze, which strongly reflects the sun's heat and gives no opening for rain to lessen the intensity of the heat, and as if the earth had become iron, unfit for the sprouting of any seeds, so that it is as if nature had turned against man in answer to man's turning against God.

28.22.0.en: Instead of the rains that water the crops, the winds carry dust that destroys them and makes the air suffocating until man perishes.

28.23.0.en: And it is the opposite of what came in (v. 7): instead of victory over the enemies, defeat overtakes you and your army is scattered into dispersed bands seeking an outlet to flee from the enemies in search of safety, and they are scattered in many kingdoms in which they feel no reassurance but are always anxious and troubled.

28.24.0.en: And because of the multitude of those slain in war and of the dead from epidemics and diseases, their bodies lie scattered on the ground with no one to bury them, and the birds of prey and the beasts tear at them, with no one to drive them off or chase them away, because the remnant that is left are occupied with their worries and sorrows and the affliction that surrounds them.

28.25.0.en: Here the Lord adds another group of diseases that strike them as a result of their turning away from Him, which are chronic and dangerous diseases that resist healing, and they are:

28.25.1.en: The boil (the boil of Egypt): the boil is pustules, festering sores, and abscesses. It was ascribed to Egypt because it was one of the ten plagues (the sixth plague) with which the Lord struck the Egyptians in the days of Moses, for their preventing the people of God from leaving Egypt (Ex 9:10). Hemorrhoids: a painful disease that affects the area of excretion in man.

28.25.2.en: The scab: a skin rash that disfigures the skin and makes people shun the sufferer.

28.25.3.en: The itch: scratching, which causes pain and distress to the one afflicted with it.

28.26.0.en: As a result of the multitude of calamities that surround them and their bewilderment at what happens to them, they are struck with madness and their behavior is marked by recklessness and instability, and they may also be struck with blindness as a result of the air being saturated with germs from the polluted dust, and not only bodily blindness but blindness of mind and spirit, so that they do not know how to act toward what faces them, and they live bewildered, lost in thought and will.

28.27.0.en: They become unable to see in broad daylight, that is, as a result of their confusion and bewilderment, so they stray from the right way to overcome their problems even if the way to do so is clear and evident, but walk in various ways that lead them to failure and frustration, and enemies gain mastery over them, so that they are only defeated, humiliated, and oppressed, finding no one to lend them a hand of help, neither from people nor from God, because the Lord their Savior hides His face from them for their sins and their lack of repentance.

28.28.0.en: Here is a description of the manifestations of the persecution that the people will suffer from the enemies, which are:

28.28.1.en: 1- The enemy who has conquered you invades you, and the wife whom you betrothed he takes for himself.

28.28.2.en: 2- The house that you build to live in, the enemy seizes, and he dwells in it and deprives you of it.

28.28.3.en: 3- The vineyard that you planted, you do not enjoy its fruit, for the enemy plunders it and you take nothing from it.

28.29.0.en: The enemy also seizes your livestock and your oxen and slaughters them before your eyes, and they give you nothing of what they slaughter. They take your donkey by force in your presence and you cannot do anything to recover it from them; they drive off your sheep and take them as spoil for themselves and you cannot resist them.

28.30.0.en: Your sons and daughters become captives of the enemies, and they take them into captivity under your sight, and you see them as they take them away, and you grieve with the utmost sorrow at what you see, and you have nothing but weeping until your eyes are weary and grief overtakes you over the loss of the children, without its being possible for you to do anything to rescue them from the hands of the enemies.

28.31.0.en: The crops of your plantings and all that you toiled for of the produce of your lands and the work of your hands are enjoyed by others, of the peoples who have conquered you, with whom you had no connection or acquaintance before, and you become broken and crushed all the days of your life.

28.32.0.en: What will befall you of calamities, and what your eyes will behold of the manifestations of oppression and humiliation of you and your sons, will make your mind fly away, so that you become like a madman who stumbles in his thoughts and has no control over himself.

28.33.0.en: And this is another blow of diseases in addition to what was mentioned earlier in (v. 22). For the Lord permits severe sores to afflict their knees and legs which they cannot be healed of, spreading over all parts of their bodies, so that it is hard for them to sit, stand, or walk, and any bodily activity becomes impossible for them.

28.34.0.en: You go into captivity and are subject to another people with whom neither you nor your fathers had any connection before, who force you to practice their pagan worship, so that you bow down to their gods made by hands, which are nothing but wood and stone, and even your king and your leaders become weak and are taken into captivity. This happened in the Assyrian captivity of the kingdom of Israel and then the Babylonian captivity of the kingdom of Judah.

28.35.0.en: Because of the severity of the horrors that befall you, the peoples look at you with astonishment and amazement at the humiliation you have come to, after the loftiness, exaltation, and high standing you had among the nations. And you will be the example pointed to when speaking of the utmost degrees of humiliation and degradation, and even the peoples to whom you are captive will mock you and ridicule you.

28.36.0.en: In spite of your toil and the great effort you expend in cultivating your fields, you will not reap harvests from them, because the Lord will send locusts upon you to eat them.

28.37.0.en: Likewise with the vines you plant, you will not gather their fruit nor drink of their wine, because the Lord will send worms upon you to eat them.

28.38.0.en: And with all the olive trees you have throughout your land, you will not be able to use any of their oil, because pests and diseases will strike the fruit before it ripens, and it will be scattered, spoiled, and fall to the ground.

28.39.0.en: Even your sons and daughters, you will not rejoice in having them at your side, for you will be deprived of them, because the enemy will take them captive to his country far from you.

28.40.0.en: The cricket ("locust"): the field cricket and kinds of insects that spoil plants, so that they attack the crops and ruin them and nothing of them is harvested.

28.41.0.en: After the strangers in your land were subject to your legislation and judgments, and even served you in many works of farming, drawing water, cutting wood, and tending cattle and sheep, they become the masters and rule over you, and you are brought low and become of lesser standing than those whose masters you formerly were.

28.42.0.en: And it is the opposite of what came in (v. 12). After they enjoyed material abundance, so that they lent to the peoples around them, the matter is reversed and, because of their extreme poverty, they become in need of begging from others, reaching the lowest degrees of humiliation and shame. And the strangers become the masters while the people of Israel become subject to them.

28.42.1.en: Do not be drawn to the pleasure of sin, lest its evil consequences come upon you and God be angry with you, and you lose the blessings you enjoy and lose your peace and your eternity, and instead be in great trouble and humiliation.

28.43.s.en: (3) The enemies' attack on them because of their turning away from God

28.43.0.en: The cause of all these previous curses is disobedience to the word of God, and these curses continue until they destroy man.

28.44.0.en: The calamities that befall you will be a lesson and a warning to later generations and a sign of the severity of the Lord's anger at your disobedience, and an affirmation of His authority, able to raise the one who does righteousness and punish the wicked. Indeed, the later generations will suffer from the inheritance of the painful state into which they were born or in which they grew up.

28.45.0.en: All the curses that strike them are the result of their not having been glad in the worship of the Lord and not having come to apply His commandments except under compulsion and with strain, despite the gifts the Lord had bestowed on them which made them rich, for instead of thanking Him for them, they were occupied by them away from Him and from their duties toward Him and their worship of Him.

28.45.1.en: It is truly sad that when a person's blessings and good things multiply, he is often occupied by them from his duties toward his Creator, so that all his thought is confined to how to keep them, increase them, and enjoy them at the expense of his fellowship with God. And instead of remembering God as the true giver of these blessings, his heart and mind are occupied with the material he possesses. May we never forget that all the successes we achieve in the various fields are from God's kindnesses to us, so that this increases our attachment to the Lord and we increase our thanks to Him for all His gifts.

28.46.0.en: Beginning with this verse and up to (v. 57), the Lord lists for them the troubles that the enemies will cause them if the Lord abandons them because of their turning away from His worship. The people then return to the bitter bondage they endured before, for the Lord hands them over to their enemies and they enslave and humiliate them. And instead of the abundance they enjoy in the Promised Land, they suffer hunger, nakedness, and need even of the necessities of life.

28.47.0.en: The Lord uses these enemies to discipline His people, so they come from distant places (as happened with the Babylonians, the Assyrians, the Persians, the Seleucids, and then the Romans) and swoop down on them with speed and ferocity as the eagle does when it swoops on its prey, and they are foreign nations whose language they do not know.

28.48.0.en: These enemies are hard of heart, so they respect no elder and have no pity on the young, but are violent and destroy everyone.

28.49.0.en: The invading peoples seize all the good things of the land, eating what the animals bear and what ripens of the fruits of the land, so that nothing is left to them of wheat, wine, oil, or the offspring of animals, and they suffer hunger and are exposed to death.

28.50.0.en: A siege is laid on all their cities until the fortresses, strongholds, and walls collapse, which they had been confident would be secure and protect them from the invaders. No city of theirs will be spared this siege, and they fall into the hands of their enemies.

28.51.0.en: As a result of the severity of the siege they are unable to provide the minimum of necessary food, so famines spread and hunger grows so intense that people lose the feeling of any lofty human emotions such as the emotion of fatherhood and motherhood, and they slaughter their sons to eat their flesh (2 Kgs 6:24-30).

28.52.0.en: When the enemies besiege the cities of the people of God and they are near to dying of hunger, the man who lives in luxury slaughters one of his sons to eat his flesh and begrudges his wife and the rest of his sons giving them any of the flesh of the slaughtered son. Thus their condition reaches this humiliation and hardness of heart.

28.53.0.en: The afterbirth ("placenta"): a part connected to the fetus that carries nourishment from the mother to the fetus and comes out with the newborn at birth, and is called in colloquial speech "al-khalas."

28.53.1.en: And also the woman who lives in such luxury that she would not set the sole of her foot on the ground because of her delicacy, that is, she lived in complete ease that did not require her to do any work, she too, when her hunger grows intense in the siege, is forced to eat the afterbirth that comes out in childbirth, and is also forced to slaughter her children and cook them, and does not agree that anyone share with her in eating them, not even her husband or her other children whom she has not yet slaughtered.

28.54.0.en: He affirms here that disobedience to the word of God and disrespect for His name bring many curses and plagues upon His people, and deadly diseases.

28.55.0.en: Diseases: plural of disease, that is, sickness.

28.55.1.en: The Lord returns once more and strikes them with every disease with which He had struck the Egyptians when He punished Pharaoh and his people. So there strike them the diseases and epidemics at which the people of God were terrified and afraid when they saw them afflict the Egyptians; these diseases will cling to them and be incurable.

28.56.0.en: The Lord makes them fall prey to many diseases, not only those written in this book but also many other diseases that are not mentioned here, which do their work in their bodies until they die from the horror and ravage of those diseases upon them.

28.57.0.en: The Lord's promise to their fathers to multiply their offspring was conditional on their keeping the covenant. Since they violated His commandments, He turns back and removes His blessing from them, so that they become a few men again and a nation small in number as they were before.

28.58.0.en: As the Lord's blessing was great for His people, so also His plagues will be great to destroy them.

28.59.0.en: And because of God's anger at them, He scatters them in the lands of the world, so that they live among the pagans who force them to worship idols made of stone and wood.

28.60.0.en: There shall be no rest for the sole of your foot: you shall have no settled place.

28.60.1.en: Failing of eyes: weakness of sight.

28.60.2.en: Sorrow of mind ("languishing of soul"): depression.

28.60.3.en: In your stay among the invading nations you will feel no rest, reassurance, or stability, but your eyesight will weaken from much weeping and lamenting over the way your circumstances have gone, and you will find no pleasure in the delights of life, for depression and distress will possess you as a result of the calamities and sorrows.

28.61.0.en: And you will be threatened with death at any moment, so you will live in fear and terror, not safe for your lives, neither by day nor by night.

28.62.0.en: You will not feel rest at any moment of your life, whether by day or by night. For from the many dangers and diseases you endure during the day, you will wish that the day would pass quickly so that night comes, thinking that it will give you rest, but the opposite happens, for the night brings new calamities and woes, and you will go back and wish that it would pass so that the day may come and be better, but sadly your whole life will become misery.

28.63.0.en: Finally Israel will find itself once again subject to the humiliation of bondage in Egypt after the Lord brought them out of it by the hand of Moses, saying to them that they would not return to bondage again, but this promise was conditional on their obedience to the commandment, which they did not keep. So this is a warning of their return to bondage and that they will be carried to Egypt in ships as captives, where they will be offered for sale as slaves and people from the other nations will not come forward to buy them, because they are not suitable in their view as slaves, for their leanness and weakness from the diseases and troubles they endured.

28.63.1.en: This is a terrible picture of the height of what they will suffer of pains and troubles that are hard to describe.

28.63.2.en: And this happened when Egypt attacked the land of the Jews and captured King Jehoahaz, and also when the Jews fled to Egypt at the Babylonian invasion and the destruction of Jerusalem, and at the attack of Titus the Roman in the year 70 AD and his killing of the Jews, some of them were sent to Egypt.

28.63.3.en: Persevere in your striving against sin, and you will enjoy God's help and fellowship and then the Kingdom of Heaven; this striving is restful and attractive, whereas the pains resulting from sin are beyond endurance and their result is perdition in eternal torment.
